display.purpose: The single h1 per route: the home thesis and every PageHeader title. Always text-balance, held to the measure or max-w-3xl.

headline.purpose: The h1 of a note article, sized to sit inside a reading column rather than dominate a viewport.

title.purpose: Home hero dek, the contact email address, and the mono value in a readout tile.

subtitle.purpose: A Section h2, an in-article h2, and page deks.

body.purpose: Document default set on body; prose runs at the 68ch measure with text-pretty.

body-compact.purpose: Secondary copy that sits beneath body scale without dropping to caption.

label.purpose: The one small-uppercase recipe (.label): section group names, dates, tags, footer column heads. Mono, ink-soft, 0.14em tracking.

reading.purpose: Any reported number: readout values, publication years, durations. Mono with tabular figures, via .font-mono-fig.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Colour-state transitions: nav hover, button fill, link tone.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Transform transitions: the link-underline scale-in and image hover scale.

motion.name: duration-reveal
motion.purpose: The single scroll-reveal fade and 8px rise.

motion.name: reveal-distance
motion.purpose: Vertical offset of a reveal's hidden state.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: House easing for reveals and every hover transition.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Symmetric easing token available for two-way state changes.

notes: globals.css is deliberately three-tier: tier 1 :root primitives are the normative tokens, tier 2 @theme inline maps semantics to Tailwind v4 utilities, tier 3 @layer base/utilities holds behavior. Components consume tier 2 only.
Light only. No dark palette exists; adding one is a brand decision, not a default.

Tier 2 also carries legacy aliases (--color-background, --color-foreground, --color-muted, --color-border) kept so pre-rebuild components keep compiling. They are compile shims, not semantics; new work uses the ground/ink/line names.
Header chrome is drawn at a literal 5px radius rather than the 6px --radius token. Consistent within the header, but a leftover literal; new surfaces use var(--radius).

src/components/primitives/Eyebrow.tsx survives from the pre-rebuild editorial system: an eyebrow/kicker at a hardcoded 10px / 0.24em on the legacy text-muted alias. It is imported nowhere and is not part of this system; .label is the only small-uppercase recipe.

src/app/opengraph-image.tsx still renders the rejected cream-plus-warm-ink palette (#f7f3ea ground, #1a1714 ink). That is a build defect against the thesis, not a token; the social card should be brought onto ground/ink.

narrative.northStar: The Instrument Panel, Read in Daylight
narrative.overview:
This is the canon played straight. The owner was offered an invented visual world (a phased-array lattice, direction seed af8c32fb) and took the standing exit instead: convention executed at full craft fidelity, no invented metaphor, no smuggled quirk. What that produces is a warm-neutral daylight panel — near-white ground, near-black ink, hairline rules, and exactly one instrument blue — where every measured value is set in monospace so numbers read as readings rather than as decoration. The register is a lab bench in a bright room, not a terminal in a dark one.

Density is calm and generous. Content sits at a 68ch measure inside a 72rem container, sections are separated by hairlines rather than cards, and vertical rhythm comes from a small 4px-based scale used at the coarse end (3rem, 4rem, 6rem) far more often than the fine end. Depth is not simulated: there are no shadows in the system, so hierarchy is carried entirely by rule weight, ink tone, and space. Motion is short and precise (140-200ms for state, 480ms for a single reveal) and focus is treated as a first-class visible state, not an afterthought to be removed.

Two rejections are confirmed and load-bearing. The site refuses the engineer-portfolio rut of a dark terminal with neon monospace, and it refuses the cream-plus-serif editorial default this site itself used before the rebuild. The craft bar is linear.app's level of finish, light only, taken as a standard of precision rather than as a look to clone; the long-form-editorial, interactive-explainer, and print-press idioms (craigmod.com, ciechanow.ski, stripe.com/press) are named rejections.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-neutral near-white ground (#fcfcfb), never cream, never dark.
One typeface for everything (Archivo) plus one mono (JetBrains Mono) restricted to labels and measured values.
Hairline rules and tonal grounds instead of shadows and cards.
A single accent, one instrument blue, spent almost entirely on primary action and focus.
Three-tier token architecture: primitives, semantic mapping, behavior — components touch only the middle tier.
Motion and reveals are opt-in for users who allow motion; content is never JavaScript-dependent to be readable.

rules.name: The Two Rules Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with exactly two line weights, both hairlines: line for anything the eye passes over (dividers, section boundaries) and line-strong for anything a finger can hit. There is no third border colour and no thicker rule.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: The accent appears on the primary action and the focus ring. It is not used to colour body links, headings, icons, hovers on text, or decorative fills. If a screen shows more than one blue element at rest, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Ink Ladder Rule
rules.body: Text tone descends in exactly three steps — ink for what is said, muted for what supports it, soft for what annotates it. Nothing is lighter than ink-soft, and no text tone is invented between the rungs.

rules.name: The No Raw Hex Rule
rules.body: Components may only use the mapped Tailwind colour utilities (bg-ground, text-ink-muted, border-line, bg-accent, …). Raw hex in a component is a defect even when the value matches a token; globals.css tier 1 is the only place a colour literal is written.

rules.name: The Mono Is A Reading Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved for measured values and labels. It never sets prose, headings, navigation, or button text. If mono appears somewhere that isn't reporting a value or naming a group, it is decoration and must come out.

rules.name: The One Label Recipe Rule
rules.body: All uppercase small type is .label — one font, one size, one tracking, one colour. There is no second small-caps style, no per-page label variant, and no locally tuned tracking or 10px size.

rules.name: The Non-Jitter Rule
rules.body: Numerals that stack in a column must not shift between rows: use .font-mono-fig or .tabular (or a real <time>) for anything numeric that repeats down a list.

rules.name: The One H1 Rule
rules.body:
PageHeader owns the single h1 of a route. A Section contributes an h2 only through its title prop, which renders a real heading wired to the section via aria-labelledby; the label prop renders a plain

and outranks nothing. A group name that must sit above inner h3s is passed as title, never as label.

rules.name: The Hairline Boundary Rule
rules.body: Sections are separated by a single bottom hairline on the section itself, not by background changes, gaps, or cards. The page reads as one continuous sheet ruled into bands.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Any run of prose gets .measure (68ch). Headings may exceed it only via an explicit max-w-3xl; body text never runs the full container width.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Surfaces do not lift. No shadows, no glows, no offset borders, no gradients. If a surface needs to separate from the page, use a hairline or a tonal ground — in that order.

rules.name: The Barely-Rounded Rule
rules.body: 6px on controls, 10px on media, 2px on focus, 0 everywhere else. A radius above 10px does not exist in this world, and neither does a pill.

dos: Do edit tier 1 of globals.css and only tier 1 when the world changes; tier 2 maps semantics to utilities and tier 3 holds behavior.
Do use only the mapped colour utilities in components (bg-ground, text-ink-soft, border-line-strong, bg-accent).

Do reach for the ruled list (ul.divide-y.divide-line.border-y.border-line with flex flex-wrap items-baseline justify-between rows, title left, mono value or label right) for any set of comparable items.

Do pass a group name to Section as title when it must outrank inner h3s; label renders only a

and creates no heading.
Do set every reported number in .font-mono-fig / .tabular so figures stay tabular and columns do not jitter.
Do wrap prose in .measure (68ch) and add text-pretty to paragraphs, text-balance to display headings.
Do keep transitions at var(--duration-fast) (140ms) for colour state and var(--duration-base) (200ms) for transforms, on var(--ease-out).
Do let focus show: the 2px accent outline is a system component, and .link-underline must fire on :focus-visible as well as hover.
Do keep content visible without JavaScript and without motion — reveals stay opt-in behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference with the <noscript> un-hide intact.
donts: Don't write a raw hex value in a component, even a correct one.
Don't add a dark palette. This site is light only by a standing brand commitment from the owner; adding dark mode is a brand decision, not a sensible default.
Don't use monospace for prose, headings, navigation, or button labels — mono means "this is a reading".
Don't invent a second small-uppercase style. If small uppercase type is needed, it is .label.
Don't add shadows, glows, gradients, or offset borders to create depth; use a hairline or ground-sunk.
Don't spend the accent on body links, headings, or decorative fills — primary action and focus only.
Don't build a card grid where a ruled list will do, and don't box a section in a border to separate it.
Don't exceed a 10px radius or introduce a new radius literal; use var(--radius) / var(--radius-lg).
Don't let a paragraph run the full 72rem container width.
Don't drive stagger from JavaScript timers; pass --reveal-delay.
Don't reach for cream grounds, serif display faces, or the dark-terminal-with-neon-mono idiom. Both are named, confirmed rejections.
